findings.evidence: `FiniteTypeTrivial.lean:122` and `:129` state the wrappers after `B : CommAlgCat.{w} R`; the source theorem in `Trivial.lean:113` has `variable {B : Type w}` while `A` is `Type v`, so the same-universe restriction is not needed.
findings.fix: Use the already-declared second universe for one value algebra, e.g. `variable (A : CommAlgCat.{v} R)` and later `variable {A : CommAlgCat.{v} R} {B : CommAlgCat.{w} R}`.
findings.issue: `B : CommAlgCat.{w} R` forces `trivialPointsMulEquiv_mapValue` and `mapValue_trivialPointsMulEquiv_symm_apply` to have same-universe value algebras, while the inherited raw theorem is universe-polymorphic in the source and target algebras.

summary: The finite-type trivial object itself is at the expected same-universe level, but the new value-algebra naturality wrappers unnecessarily restrict source and target algebras to the same universe.
